newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO CETES RATE UP ON SOFT PESO, U.S. LONG BOND.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO CETES RATE UP ON SOFT PESO, U.S. LONG BOND.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were up 100 basis points at 19.75 percent in late morning trade on Friday under pressure from a weak peso and rising yields on the U.S. long bond, dealers said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts had weakened 1.65 centavos to 7.8260/7.8290 per dollar while the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was down 38/32 to yield 6.62 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper were up 125 basis points to 21.25 percent.
Liquidity of 964 million pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.

Banco de Mexico drained 2.449 billion pesos from the market through three direct Cetes sales and five repos, which dealers said the central bank assigned at high rates. Overnight rates on bank paper declined 25 basis points to 20.25 percent.
Liquidity of 1.073 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system on Monday from prior central bank participation.
